changes.summary: Architecture as a medium for national expression: from palaces to urban mansions, 19th-century decoration reflects history and celebrates grandeur. At the turn of the century, its initial vocation stepped aside to give way to freer forms of embellishment. In the 19th century, decoration of buildings was a means of conveying images of history and messages on the nation’s vitality by reaching a wide audience All forms of architecture were involved: regal edifices such as the Louvre, banks, commercial buildings and urban mansions where architects competed to created sophisticated interiors. With the advent of rationalism and Art Nouveau, such decorations no longer aimed to establish links with history and either became picturesque or naturalistic.
